title: CLI, SDK and player: make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: EPIC
Spec section(s): all (§0-§16)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-04): "We need a CLI for this" (idea #1: run the video loop locally with your own agent) and "we want
proper CLI that uses proper SDK and we can add to docs section" (idea #14, which includes the player). One plan for all
of it: the CLI's remote commands are built only on the SDK, and local mode is a CLI command.

What ships (§0): three public npm packages, one private workspace package, a few server changes.
- netlify-video-agent-sdk: typed client for a deployment's REST API. Resource methods GENERATED from the OpenAPI spec
  using an explicit x-sdk name per route (va.videos.create, va.versions.publish…), plus hand-written helpers for
  multi-request jobs (wait, download, upload, music jobs, webhooks, feature checks).
- netlify-video-agent (bin video-agent): remote commands over the SDK, with --json and stable exit codes for agents;
  and `video-agent local …`, which makes a video ON YOUR MACHINE with Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI inside that
  agent's OS sandbox, with no Netlify account.
- netlify-video-agent-player: <video-agent-player>, a small web component for published videos (later phase, in scope).
- packages/action: private workspace package owned by the github-action plan; never published to npm.
Plus /docs/cli and /docs/sdk under a docs navigation that scales; `video-agent login` (approve in the browser, get an
API key); operationIds + x-sdk on every route; version + features in GET /api/v1/config; /v/{slug}.json.

Positioning (owner decision 2026-11-04): "make one locally, then deploy it for your team". Local mode is the front
door; review, editor, publishing, API/MCP, queue, planning and the shared library stay hosted (§6.7). Every local run
ends with one line pointing at the Deploy to Netlify button.

This plan is the HUB for the five other 2026-11-04 plans (§12): it owns the features registry, operationIds/x-sdk and
the coverage test, the SDK, the CLI catalog and exit-code rule, packages/ workspaces + Changesets + trusted publishing,
local mode's runtime bundle (prepare-run --inputs), and the docs navigation. Other plans add their own routes, SDK
helpers (redoScenes, uploadRecording), CLI commands (scenes/redo, looks/restyle, --engine, demo, record, brief) and
docs pages on top of this groundwork, in their own beads.

Reviews: independent Fable 5.1, cross-plan seam review, remote Fable 5.1 high in a Netlify Agent Run (all "sound with
changes"; logs in §16). Key changes they forced: names (video-agent and @video-agent are taken), OS sandbox as the
boundary (tool allowlists aren't), keys can't create keys (device flow mints at claim), file: callback instead of a
loopback server, local mode decoupled from render-engines, nothing on npmjs before the repo is public.

Owner questions (§13):
- Q1 DECIDED (2026-11-04): unscoped names netlify-video-agent (CLI, bin video-agent), netlify-video-agent-sdk,
  netlify-video-agent-player; no npm org (the @video-agent scope is someone else's).
- Q2 DECIDED (2026-11-04): ship local mode, framed "make one locally, then deploy it for your team".
- Q3 open: CLI login on every deployment by default? BUILDING: yes, with the cliLoginEnabled admin switch.
- Q4 open: where keys live? BUILDING: a 0600 config file; CI uses VIDEO_AGENT_KEY or --key - --no-save.
- Q5 open: local push to the team app? BUILDING: not in v1 (design in Considerations).
- Q6 open: publishing before the repo is public? BUILDING: npm pack tarballs internally; first npmjs publish from the
  public repo with provenance.
- Q7 open: /player.js served by every deployment? BUILDING: yes.
- Q8 open: an agent that can't finish inside its sandbox in C2? BUILDING: leave it out of v1 (Gemini is the likely one).
- Q9 open: server-side wait (rest_wait)? BUILDING: not in v1; If-None-Match polling.
Other owner decisions applied: live tests run --dry then ask the owner before each gate (no blanket approval).

## Approach
Phases (§11), each ending in a gate bead; gates chain where the plan says so:
0 spikes C1-C4 (bundled runtime, sandboxed agents, Kokoro venv, npm placeholders); 1 API groundwork (operationIds +
x-sdk, version + features, request ids, oasdiff warning job, workspaces, /v/{slug}.json); 2 the SDK; 3 the CLI's remote
commands + device login; 4 local mode; 5 the player; 6 docs, nav and README; 7 release.
Parallelism: phases 0 and 1 together; then 2, 4 (needs C1-C3 and 3.1 only) and 5 together; the rest of 3 after 2.
Live tests (LT-1 SDK, LT-2 CLI, LT-3 local with real agents) are their own gate beads and block the release gate.

## Done when
Every phase epic closed; LT-1..LT-3 passed with owner approval; CI green; the fresh-machine check (7.3) passes; the plan
gets an as-built note (deviations, credits spent).

## Tests
Per bead. Live tests: scripts/e2e/sdk.ts, scripts/e2e/cli.ts (production, owner-approved, credit ceilings), and a manual
local-mode run per shipped agent (tester's own subscriptions). CI: a fixture-agent local-mode job (4.8).

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

## Considerations
Not in v1, designed (§14), so nothing is lost:
- local preview <dir> (unpack source, npx hyperframes preview --background = HyperFrames Studio); local render <dir>
  (render-unchanged run without an agent, render-job only); local init (writes ./context/ BRAND.md template, brand.json,
  assets/, and video-agent.json defaults: agent, aspect, sound, output folder); local list (videos under ./videos/).
- Named profiles: profiles list|use|remove, --profile, VIDEO_AGENT_PROFILE, config { current, profiles: { <name>: {
  url, apiKey, keyId } } }.
- CLI `webhooks verify --secret <s> [--signature <h>] < body` (exit 0/1) and `music search|import` commands (the SDK
  methods ship in v1).
- Runtime matrix beyond Node 22/24: Deno, Bun, a Vite-bundled browser smoke test.
- local push: import API taking a local source.tar.gz + outputs, verified server-side with a render-unchanged run (Q5).
- LocalRunnerPort for netlify dev: RUNNER=local only with ALLOW_NON_PRODUCTION=true; start spawns the local executor
  with the server's own prompt, snapshot reads the child, stop uses proc-tree. The file half (prepare-run --inputs)
  ships in v1; the other half needs render-job's already-typed `signed` upload mode (prompt.ts:22, :112, not
  implemented in render-job) plus dev-only upload/fetch endpoints, because netlify blobs:get/set hit the linked
  project's real stores, not netlify dev's emulated ones.
- Native Windows (WSL works; config would live under %APPDATA%).
- rest_wait: ?wait=<0-10> on GET /api/v1/videos/{id}, reusing the MCP loop (src/mcp.ts:541-545), honouring
  If-None-Match; 60 s sync function limit makes 10 s safe; billed function time, so measure against If-None-Match
  polling (requests and GB-s per finished video) and ship only on a clear win; advertised as rest_wait (reserved string).
- Interactive terminal planning (arrow-key choices, write-ins, skip, accept the brief); v1 prints questions and takes
  --answers.
- local --engine remotion (after render-engines phase 2 and its licence decision): refuses without
  --accept-remotion-license, prints that plan's notice once; runtime bundle carries engines/remotion/template/ (lockfile
  only; npm ci at run time with registry.npmjs.org added to the sandbox network allowlist).
- --pass-env NAME for ELEVENLABS_API_KEY / OPENVERSE_CLIENT_*: passes one variable and adds its host to the allowlist;
  out of v1 because it puts a secret where an injected instruction could read it.
- Player extras: hover-preview (muted hover clip from /v/{slug}.json `hover`), theming (::part(video), ::part(credits),
  --va-player-radius, --va-player-background).
- CLI variants of every skill recipe (changelog, social cut, localise, review).
- Plan-with-questions locally; the browser editor locally; Python/Go SDKs; a React wrapper for the player; admin
  commands beyond `api`; OAuth for REST; the OS keychain; telemetry of any kind.
Risks (§15): agent CLI flags drift (live test checks --help); sandboxes differ by OS (C2 on macOS and Linux; doctor
explains); local failures runners don't have (doctor, --keep, agent.log, run.jsonl); bundle drift (fixture CI job runs
the bundle); prompt injection via inputs (fences + sandbox + deny lists + env scrub + network allowlist); device-flow
phishing and lockout; settings that quietly reopen the host (allowLocalBinding, broad Seatbelt profiles: never set);
no spend cap for Codex/Gemini subscriptions (max-turns, timeouts); monorepo install time (hoisted devDeps, measured);
support load (stated matrix); Netlify positioning (decided: ship).

title: C2: spike each agent CLI headless inside its OS sandbox (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: C2
Spec section(s): §11 Phase 0 C2; §6.5; §1 Agent CLIs; §2 gotchas 10-11

## Background
The reviews established that a tool allowlist is not a boundary (Write + Bash(npx tsx scripts/*) is arbitrary code;
Read/cat reach ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.netlify and the CLI's own config holding an nva_ key) and that the person's own agent
config (hooks, MCP servers/connectors, plugins, memory files) loads into a run unless suppressed. The OS sandbox is the
boundary. Claude Code's sandbox wraps Bash only; Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep run in-process under permission rules. On
Linux a sandboxed command's localhost is private; macOS Seatbelt allows only the sandbox proxy; allowLocalBinding
(macOS only) reopens every localhost service and is never set. Gemini headless auto_edit denies every shell command,
workspace policy files don't apply, and its default macOS profile permissive-open allows broad reads and all network.
Codex workspace-write blocks network by default. `-p --output-format stream-json` requires --verbose in Claude Code.
Flags seen on the author's machine (2026-11-04): claude 2.1.280 (--verbose, --permission-mode dontAsk, --settings,
--setting-sources, --strict-mcp-config, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd), codex-cli 0.157.1 (exec, -s, -C,
--skip-git-repo-check, --json, -o, -c, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox), gemini (-p, --approval-mode,
-s/--sandbox, -o stream-json, undocumented --policy).

## Approach
With the C1 workspace and the real buildPrompt output, run each agent twice: a silent 15 s video, then a narrated one
with music, using the §6.5 settings:
- Claude Code: claude -p <prompt> --verbose --output-format stream-json --permission-mode dontAsk --setting-sources ""
  --strict-mcp-config --max-turns <n> --settings <ws>/.va/claude.json (sandbox.enabled, failIfUnavailable,
  allowUnsandboxedCommands false, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, sandbox.network.allowedDomains, sandbox.filesystem.denyRead,
  plus permissions.deny for the same paths and for Read/Glob/Grep outside the workspace; allow Bash, Read, Write, Edit,
  Glob, Grep; deny WebFetch, WebSearch). Linux needs bubblewrap + socat.
- Codex: codex exec -C <ws> --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --sandbox workspace-write
  -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -c 'shell_environment_policy.inherit="none"'
  -c 'shell_environment_policy.set={…}' --json -o <ws>/.render/last.txt, deny-read permissions, no user MCP config.
- Gemini: gemini -p <prompt> --sandbox --approval-mode yolo -o stream-json, custom Seatbelt profile on macOS, Docker or
  Podman on Linux with only the workspace mounted, a workspace-only settings home; never write ~/.gemini/policies.
Deny-read list: ~/.ssh ~/.aws ~/.config/gcloud ~/.azure ~/.netlify ~/.npmrc ~/.config/video-agent ~/.codex ~/.gemini
~/.claude (except what the agent needs to authenticate before the sandboxed shell starts) ~/.docker ~/.kube ~/.gnupg.
Network allowlist: api.openverse.org + Openverse audio hosts (Jamendo, Freesound, Wikimedia Commons), the HyperFrames
model hosts (from C3), the agent's own API host.
Canaries: a file in a deny-read folder (try `cat` AND the agent's own Read tool), a canary env var, and a canary HTTP
server on the host's 127.0.0.1.

## Done when
Per agent and OS: finished or not, minutes, blocked commands/hosts, final settings, canaries held. Pass for an agent:
finishes both videos sandboxed and every canary held (the loopback canary confirms the file: handoff is the only path
back). An agent that fails doesn't ship in v1 (Q8 default); expect Claude Code and Codex to ship, Gemini at risk.
Results feed 4.4b-4.4d exactly (settings files, flags, allowlist hosts). Spends the tester's own subscriptions only.

## Background
The spec has no operationIds (grep -c operationId ui/src/api/openapi.json = 0). Routes use createRoute({ method, path,

an explicit per-route SDK name (review A3, owner constraint: generated names must read well), never derived from paths
or operationIds, so naming is a decision a reviewer sees in the route's diff.

  reviseVideo, remixVideo, retryVersion, cancelVersion, publishVersion, unpublishVersion, setVerdict, uploadMedia,
  createUploadSession, checkMedia, listKeys, revokeKey, getConfig, getMe…), and an `x-sdk` extension

  routes at src/app.ts:539, :557; media.check for POST /api/v1/media/check at :1436), or `x-sdk: false` for routes the
  SDK doesn't expose as a method (internal run callbacks /api/internal/runs/{id}/done and /checkpoint at :2215, :2243;

  value; no two operations share { resource, method }. Regenerate openapi.json (npm run openapi:gen).

Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.1
Spec section(s): §4.1 layers 1-2, Generated signature rule; §4.3

## Background
Today openapi:gen writes ui/src/api/openapi.json then runs openapi-typescript@7.13.0 into ui/src/api/schema.d.ts
(package.json scripts). Generation wins for coverage and drift: a new route is in the SDK the day it merges, typed
(review A3). One generated schema shared with the UI so they can't disagree.

## Approach
- openapi:gen: openapi-typescript once into packages/sdk/src/generated/schema.d.ts; ui/src/api/schema.d.ts becomes a
  one-line re-export of it; then scripts/gen-sdk.ts writes packages/sdk/src/generated/resources.ts. openapi:check checks
  both generated files.
- gen-sdk.ts reads each operation's x-sdk { resource, method } and emits one namespace per resource, one thin typed
  method per operation. Signature rule: path params positionally in path order, then one `input` object (body fields
  and query fields merged; generation FAILS if a body field and a query field share a name), then opts
  ({ idempotencyKey?, signal?, headers? }). Examples: va.versions.publish(id, n, { transcript: true }),
  va.videos.list({ mine: true, search: 'webhooks' }), va.versions.retry(id, n). Binary-body routes (small media upload)
  are skipped (hand-written). x-sdk: false routes are skipped (reachable via raw).
- Pageable marker: an operation is pageable only when its 200 response has items + nextCursor (RecordingListSchema,
  src/schemas.ts:911, has none), recorded for listAll's types (2.3a).
- Exported convenience types: Video, Version, Media, Plan, Comment, WebhookEvent derived from paths as
  ui/src/api/client.ts derives Video/Version.

## Done when
Generated files committed and checked in CI; UI typechecks against the re-export; generator deterministic.

## Tests
Generator unit tests on a small fixture spec (positional params, merged input, name-clash failure, x-sdk false, pageable detection); determinism (two runs equal); openapi:check fails on stale generated files.

Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: LT-1
Spec section(s): §11 Phase 2 gate (live part)

## Background
Checks the SDK end to end on the real deployment: uploads, waits and downloads behave on Netlify, not just in fakes.

## Approach
New scripts/e2e/sdk.ts (header comment lists every variable and check, like scripts/e2e/remix.ts): read-only checks with
VIDEO_ID (get, list, listAll, files.url for every file kind, download and verify an MP4 with ffprobe); a media upload
over 4 MB through a session and its deletion in finally; music search; with CREATE_OK=1 one 10-second video created,
waited for, downloaded and verified (~150 credits). CREDIT_CEILING default 300.

Live test rule (owner decision 2026-11-04): a live test is a script that makes real videos on the production site and checks them; it costs credits. Run it with --dry first (prints the steps and the projected credits, spends nothing), then ASK THE OWNER for a go-ahead before running it for real, every time. Never pre-approved, never in CI. It stops at its CREDIT_CEILING and deletes what it made (test media, test videos where possible, publications) in a finally.

## Done when
Dry run shown to the owner; owner approved; run passed; credits spent recorded in the plan.

## Tests
Structured JSON-line log per step (request ids, ms, credits so far); exits non-zero on the first failed check, after cleanup.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

title: SDK core: VideoAgent client, auth, raw, redirects, errors, retries, idempotency, logger, User-Agent
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.2
Spec section(s): §4.2; §2 gotchas 17, 17a

## Background
Behaviour every method shares. Facts: keys start nva_ (src/domain/auth.ts:88); errors are { error: { code, message } }
(ui/src/api/client.ts ApiErrorBody); rate limits answer rate_limited with Retry-After: 60 (src/app.ts:180);
Idempotency-Key accepted on create/revise/remix (src/app.ts:139, :334, :471, :498, :1233); the server hashes
JSON.stringify(body) and answers 409 conflict when a key returns with a different hash (src/domain/videos.ts:280-284),
TTL 24 h per user and operation (:54); file routes 302 to signed storage URLs valid 5-10 minutes (src/app.ts:676-707).

## Approach
- new VideoAgent({ url (or VIDEO_AGENT_URL), apiKey (or VIDEO_AGENT_KEY when process exists), userAgent?, fetch?,
  retries = 3, logger? }). User-Agent: netlify-video-agent-sdk/<version> (+<userAgent>).
- raw: openapi-fetch (MIT, bundled into dist; no runtime deps) typed by generated paths, with auth, base URL, retries,
  errors.
- Redirects: authenticated requests use redirect: 'manual' and never follow with the key (file routes handled by 2.3b).
- Idempotency: create/revise/remix (and later redoScenes) send Idempotency-Key (opts.idempotencyKey or a UUID). The body
  is serialized ONCE and the same string is sent on every retry; a 409 on a retry is reported, never retried.
- Retries: GETs and keyed POSTs on network errors, 429 (Retry-After capped at 60 s) and 5xx, jittered backoff; other
  POSTs never retry.
- Errors: VideoAgentError { status, code, message, retryAfterSec?, requestId? (x-nf-request-id) }; isVideoAgentError(e,
  code).
- Logger: (event, fields) => void with request events (method, path, status, ms, attempt, requestId); never headers or
  bodies.
- No Node-only imports in the main entry.

## Done when
Client constructs from options or env; raw and generated methods authenticate, retry, map errors and log as specified.

## Tests
Unit: retries/backoff with fake timers, Retry-After, key reuse and identical bytes across retries (assert body string equality), 409-on-retry not retried, error mapping incl. requestId, no Authorization on any followed redirect, logger never sees headers/bodies (grep for nva_). Integration: in-process app via fetch: (req) => app.fetch(req) with createApp(makeDeps(...), { isLive: () => true }).

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. title: SDK helpers: videos.wait (If-None-Match, no default timeout) and listAll
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.3a
Spec section(s): §4.2 Waiting; §4.1 videos row; §1 ETags

## Background
GET /api/v1/videos/{id} sets an etag including the signed URLs' expiry and answers 304 to a matching If-None-Match
(src/app.ts:410-424). Statuses: queued, running, finishing, ready, failed, cancelled, timed_out (src/schemas.ts:62).
Review R6: no default timeout, because a run may use the runner's full 25 minutes, retries re-queue, and with
MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS 3 a queued video can wait longer than any fixed default; a default that gave up fails healthy CI. There
is no queue-position field in the API. rest_wait (server-side wait) is not in v1.

## Approach
- videos.wait(id, { version?, timeoutMs?, intervalMs?, onProgress?, signal? }): poll with If-None-Match (304 = no
  change), every 3 s for the first minute then 8 s (intervalMs overrides). onProgress(status, stage, step) from
  /api/v1/videos/{id}/progress when the etag changes (status includes queued). Resolves on ready; throws
  VideoAgentError code video_failed (with status and version error) on failed, cancelled, timed_out. timeoutMs and
  signal stop it (CLI --timeout → exit 6).
- listAll(method, input): async iterator over nextCursor, typed so it only accepts pageable operations (2.1 marker).

## Done when
wait handles 304s, every terminal status, progress callbacks, signal and timeout; listAll iterates pages and is a type error on non-pageable lists.

## Tests
In-process integration moving the fake attempt to ready, failed, timed_out; 304 path asserted; fake timers for cadence; type test (tsd/expect-type) for listAll on RecordingList.

title: SDK helpers: files.url and files.download (DTO-signed vs 302, no Authorization on storage fetch)
description:

## Background

(src/domain/videos.ts:955, :962-990); video, captions, narration audio and transcript are unsigned API links that 302
(:942-946) to storage URLs valid 5-10 minutes (src/app.ts:680). The edge function accepts signed URLs up to an hour

## Approach
files.url(video, { file, version? }): DTO-signed files return straight from the DTO (no request); others request the
file route with redirect: 'manual', read Location, return it. files.download(video, { file, version?, to? }): same
split; fetch the storage URL immediately WITHOUT Authorization; in Node with `to`, stream to disk via dynamic node:fs
import (temp file + rename); elsewhere return the Response. Files: video, poster, gif, captions, narration, transcript,
previews.

## Done when
Both helpers work for every file kind; the key never reaches the storage host; downloads are atomic on disk.

Unit: redirect handling asserts no Authorization header on the second fetch; DTO-signed files make zero requests; partial download leaves no file. Integration against the in-process app plus a stub storage fetch.

title: SDK helpers: media.upload (sessions, resume, wait for ready), music.importAndWait, config.get/supports
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.3c
Spec section(s): §4.1 media/music/config rows; §2 gotchas 12, 16

## Background
POST /api/v1/media?filename=&caption= takes up to 4 MB; bigger files use upload sessions with parts of at most 4 MB,
each with its own sha256, then complete (src/domain/media-uploads.ts:2, :22 PART_SIZE, :148-149;
skills/netlify-video/references/connect.md:67-81); an item must reach status ready (or rejected with rejectReason).
Openverse imports may answer 202 with a job to poll. Screen recordings are the big-upload case (screen plan adds
media.uploadRecording on top of this).

## Approach
- media.upload(file | path | Blob, { caption?, role?, onProgress?, signal? }): ≤4 MB → single POST; else create a
  session, slice 4 MB parts, sha256 each (WebCrypto), PUT parts with retries, resume by listing received parts after a
  failure, complete, then poll GET /api/v1/media/{id} until ready (or throw VideoAgentError code media_rejected with
  rejectReason). Uses media.check(hashes) first to skip uploading a file already in the library.
- music.importAndWait(openverseId): follows the 202 job until done/failed.
- config.get() cached once per client; config.supports(feature); methods for newer features throw
  VideoAgentError code unsupported_by_server naming the feature and server version.

## Done when
Uploads of any size succeed, resume after a forced failure, and wait for ready; music jobs complete; feature checks work.

## Tests
Unit: part slicing and hashes against media-uploads.ts rules, resume after a dropped part, rejected item, check-first dedupe; integration with the in-process app and the fakes' media assembly; unsupported_by_server when the fake config lacks a feature.

title: SDK webhooks: verifyWebhook and parseWebhook (WebCrypto, raw body, delivery headers)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec key: 2.4
Spec section(s): §4.1 top-level row; §4.2 Webhooks

## Background
Signatures are t=<unix>,v1=<hex>, hex = HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" (src/lib/crypto.ts:44-46). Deliveries also
carry x-video-agent-event and x-video-agent-delivery (src/domain/webhooks.ts:189-191); receivers dedupe on eventId.

## Approach
verifyWebhook({ secret, body (raw string), signature, toleranceSec = 300 }): parse, constant-time compare via
crypto.subtle, reject timestamps outside tolerance, malformed headers. parseWebhook({ secret, body, headers }):
verify then return the typed event with eventId, event type and delivery id. Runs on Node, Deno, Bun, Workers, Netlify
Edge (WebCrypto only).

## Done when
Both functions exported and documented; work on Node 22/24.

## Tests

title: CLI catalog, router, help, --json, exit codes, logging and config file
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 3.1
Spec section(s): §6.1; §6.2 Config, Exit codes, Logging

## Background
Single source of truth for commands, like src/mcp-catalog.ts for MCP tools. No framework: node:util parseArgs plus a
catalog router, bundled into one file (record's Playwright is the one exception, owned by screen-recording). Needed by
local mode (phase 4) as well as remote commands.

## Approach
- packages/cli/src/catalog.ts: per command name, summary, args, flags (types, defaults), examples, SDK methods used,
  required features string (hidden when the server doesn't list it), needsHostedApp. Router, --help, help --json from it.
- Output: --json prints exactly one JSON object on stdout; progress and prompts on stderr. Errors with --json:
  { error: { code, message, requestId? } } on stdout too.
- Exit codes, mapped by HTTP status first, then specific codes override: 0 ok; 1 error (5xx, network, unmapped); 2 usage
  or invalid request (bad flags; 400: invalid_request, unknown_look, look_not_allowed…); 3 401; 4 403/404; 5 code
  video_failed; 6 wait --timeout; 7 409 (conflict, not_editable, remix_disabled, look_disabled, engine_disabled,
  engine_unsupported, cli_login_disabled, narration lock); 8 429; 9 unsupported_by_server. A new server code needs no
  CLI change unless it should override its status's exit code (shared rule).
- Config: one profile in v1, ~/.config/video-agent/config.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME honoured), mode 0600,
  { url, apiKey, keyId, webhookSecret? }. Precedence: flags > VIDEO_AGENT_URL/VIDEO_AGENT_KEY > file.

description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec key: 3.3a
Spec section(s): §5.2 (all bullets)

## Background
A device-style flow (RFC 8628 model) that ends in an ordinary API key: no OAuth config needed, works with Identity and
Sign in with Netlify, and the key appears (and can be revoked) on the API keys page. Facts: createKey refuses non-session
principals (src/domain/keys.ts:17-20) and returns key AND webhookSecret once (:35); using a key re-checks the owner
(disabled, domain no longer allowed: src/domain/auth.ts:100-108; Identity user gone/unconfirmed: :134-139); keys are
compared with safeEqual on sha256 (auth.ts:129). Reviews: mint at claim (no key at rest), owner checks at claim, return
webhookSecret, typed code (RFC 8628 §5.4), caps against lockout. Nothing in the app limits by IP yet (new work).
Migration order (roadmap): after redo-a-scene's phase-2 migration, before screen-recording's.

## Approach
- Migration: cli_logins (id, device_code_hash, user_code 8 chars unambiguous alphabet shown ABCD-EFGH, label ≤64
  printable ASCII, host ≤64, client_ip, status pending|approved|denied|claimed|expired, user_id, api_key_id,
  failed_attempts, created_at, expires_at = +10 min); settings.cliLoginEnabled (default true) with the admin settings
  schema. Drizzle schema + db:generate; memory store + PGlite store.
- src/domain/cli-login.ts: createLogin({label, host, clientIp}) → { loginId, deviceCode, userCode, verificationUrl
  (no code in it), intervalSec }; approve(principal user, userCode) records user_id/status approved (5 wrong codes per
  session → 15-minute lock; ≤10 approvals per person per hour); claim(loginId, deviceCode): safeEqual on sha256;
  pending | denied | expired | slow_down (polling faster than intervalSec) | approved → re-run the key-owner checks with
  the same helpers principalFromRequest uses (disabled, domain, Identity confirmed) → denied if any fail; else mint via
  createKeyForUser(userId, "CLI · <host> · <date>") (extract from createKey after the session check, keys.ts:21-35),
  return { apiKey, keyId, webhookSecret, user } once, status claimed.
- Limits: ≤10 pending per client IP (x-nf-client-connection-ip; count pending rows), ≤500 pending globally.
- Admin switch off → 409 cli_login_disabled. Feature string cli_login emitted when on (1.2 registry).
- Sweep: delete rows an hour after expiry.

## Done when
Domain functions and migration done; all limits and checks enforced; no key ever stored.

## Tests
Integration on memory and PGlite: happy path; wrong code lockout; approval rate limit; per-IP and global caps; slow_down; expiry; approve-then-disable → denied; approve-then-domain-removed → denied; claim returns webhookSecret once and second claim fails; switch off → cli_login_disabled; sweep. ## Background
repoRoot comes from the script location (scripts/lib/run-tools.ts:12). render-job always uploads with netlify blobs:set
(scripts/render-job.ts:358-381), then POSTs the manifest to --callback (:419-434), and derives the checkpoint URL as
/done → /checkpoint (:196); it writes .render/<attempt>/manifest.json first (:416). checkpoint.ts is best effort
(scripts/checkpoint.ts:1-5, bundle cap 2 MB :12). PromptInput.upload is { mode: 'blobs' } | { mode: 'signed'; url }
(src/domain/prompt.ts:22); buildPrompt writes the --upload arg (:112); the service always passes blobs
(reconciler.ts:225, :252, :343). The template version is recorded on the attempt (reconciler.ts:457), not in the prompt
text. A host loopback server is unreachable from the sandboxes (review R1), so files carry results back.

## Approach
1. run-tools.ts:12 → repoRoot = process.env.VA_REPO_ROOT ?? <today's value>.
2. render-job: --upload local skips Blobs uploads and uploadReferences. A --callback file://<ws>/.render/<attempt>/done
   writes done.json (the manifest) at that path instead of POSTing (410 branch n/a). postCheckpoint with a file: URL
   writes <seq>.json (message, renderPercent, optional bundle ≤2 MB) into the derived checkpoint folder. https: callbacks
   unchanged.
3. PromptInput.upload gains { mode: 'local' }; buildPrompt writes --upload local.
4. Prompt tests: for the same PromptInput, blobs and local prompts differ only in the --upload argument; a fixture blobs
   PromptInput produces exactly today's text (feature-off byte-identical rule).
5. Bump PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION by 1 in merge order (shared rule: no literal numbers; test/remix-run.test.ts:176 imports
   the constant if not already).

## Done when
Runner path byte-identical; local modes work; tests pass.

Unit: file callback writes done.json atomically; checkpoint file sequence; path refusal; prompt diff test; existing render-job tests unchanged. JSON logs for each new branch (render.upload_skipped, callback.file_written, checkpoint.file_written).

Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 4.3a
Spec section(s): §6.3 steps 1-3; §2 gotchas 8, 10

## Background
render-job's npx -y hyperframes is unpinned (render-job.ts:202); off the runner it would fetch latest with the user's
~/.npmrc. netlify-agent-kit install --force works anywhere and installs ffmpeg/ffprobe static builds, the HyperFrames
skills into .claude/skills and .agents/skills, the render Chrome and an environment skill, but writes ~/.cache and links
~/.local/bin (README) — so HOME is redirected (C1 confirms).

## Approach
- `video-agent local "<prompt>" [--agent claude|codex|gemini] [--model] [--aspect] [--duration] [--sound] [--voice]
  [--media path:"caption"…] [--context dir] [--look id|path] [--out dir] [--keep] [--timeout]`.
- Agent pick: flag, else first installed and signed in (claude, codex, gemini) among shipped adapters.
- Runtime: ~/.cache/video-agent/runtime/<cli version>/ ← npm ci from the bundled lockfile once; node_modules symlinks in
  <ws> and <ws>/video; .bin first on the child's PATH; empty npm_config_userconfig.
- Workspace ~/.cache/video-agent/runs/<run id>/ (deleted unless --keep): video/ template, context/ (--context, else
  ./context, else neutral), root AGENTS.md, scripts/<name>.ts shims to runtime/*.mjs, VA_REPO_ROOT=<ws>,
  VA_NETLIFY_CLI=off.
- Skills/tools: netlify-agent-kit install --force in <ws> with HOME=~/.cache/video-agent/agent-kit-home; that home's
  .local/bin joins PATH. (Fallback per C1: copy dist/skills from the pinned hyperframes and npx hyperframes browser.)
- --look: id resolves against looks bundled at build time (looks plan), a path points at a look folder.

## Done when
A workspace is built reproducibly; tools resolve to pinned copies; nothing touches the user's ~/.local/bin or ~/.npmrc.

## Tests
Integration on Linux CI: build a workspace, assert PATH order, symlinks, skills present, npm_config_offline second run makes no fetch; JSON-line logs per step.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. title: Local agent adapter framework: env allowlist, deny lists, network allowlist, budgets, proc-tree stop
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 4.4a
Spec section(s): §6.5 items 1-4, Deny-read list, Network allowlist, What leaves/stays

## Background
The OS sandbox is the boundary, not a tool allowlist. Killing a process group isn't enough (spike S11: npm exec and a
worker survived a group SIGTERM); scripts/lib/proc-tree.ts runs detached, samples the tree, SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs every
pid seen (proc-tree.ts:1-6).

## Approach
Adapter interface { name, detect(), signedIn(), command(ws, prompt, opts), parseEvents(stream), sandboxCheck() }.
Shared:
- Child env allowlist: PATH (runtime first), HOME, USER, LANG, TERM, TMPDIR, VA_*, RENDER_QUALITY, empty
  npm_config_userconfig, the agent's own auth vars when set. Never VIDEO_AGENT_*, NETLIFY_*, cloud credentials, any
  other secret (no --pass-env in v1).
- Deny-read list and network allowlist constants (from C2), rendered into each agent's settings.
- 30-minute default timeout (--timeout); Ctrl-C and timeout stop the tree with proc-tree.ts, never by name or group alone.
- --no-sandbox escape hatch: warns once, still scrubs env.
- Logs: agent events to agent.log, a one-line terminal status, run.jsonl steps. /docs/cli warns that agent.log, run.jsonl
  and prompt.txt hold the full prompt (brand text, captions).
- No telemetry: nothing is sent to us.

## Done when
Framework in place with a test adapter; env and stop behaviour proven.

## Tests
Unit: env filtering (canaries absent), timeout and Ctrl-C kill a fake process tree with a detached grandchild, --no-sandbox warning once.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. Ships only if C2 passed for Claude Code. Claude Code's sandbox covers Bash only; file tools need permissions.deny rules. stream-json with -p requires --verbose.

permissions.deny for those paths and for Read/Glob/Grep outside the workspace; allow Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep;
deny WebFetch, WebSearch; never allowLocalBinding. --budget <usd> maps to --max-budget-usd for API-key users. Linux:
bubblewrap + socat (doctor). Exact keys as C2 recorded.

## Background
Plays a published video on any page with the share page's guarantees: no layout shift, captions, CC BY credits always shown (the embed snippet and share page always show them: src/domain/videos.ts:852, public.ts).

shows a plain error.

title: Remix a video: a new video from another video's composition plus a change request
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: remix a video (a new video that starts from another video's finished composition plus a change request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-03-remix.md (draft 3, commit 73bea33; §0 = owner decisions from the 2026-11-03 interview, §10 = review log of the Fable 5.1 + Codex gpt-6.1-sol reviews). Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: RM
Spec section(s): all (§0-§9)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-03): from a video, press Remix, say what should change, and get a NEW video that starts from the
original's finished composition, prompts and settings rather than from scratch: a clone plus a revision. People will use
it every way, from "exactly this, swap the brand names" to "a video like this about a totally different topic".

What already exists (spec §1): every finished version keeps its whole composition as sources/{jobId}/v{n}.tar.gz
(index.html, summary.json, agent-made assets, AI voice clips, music credits; <=10 MiB tar limit; hash in
outputs.sha256, finalize.ts:217), library media as version_media snapshots (key + hash), and its settings on the
versions row. Revisions already restore a parent archive into video/ and ask the agent to change it
(reviseVideo videos.ts:369-464, reconciler.ts:252-277, prepare-run.ts:376-395). A remix is that run with three
differences: the parent is in another video, the result is a new video owned by the remixer, and some state is dropped
(recorded narration, edit state, captions).

Owner decisions (§0): no fidelity toggle (the agent infers how much to change); entry points on the video page, a Library
tile menu, the public share page (signed-in Creators only) and New video ("Start from an existing video" search picker);
optional Plan first like revisions; immediate-source lineage only; apply today's brand; source media as removable
chips; source length prefilled; language inherited (transcription only); no owner opt-out; admin kill switch
remixEnabled (on by default); empty "What would you change?" box; source comments not carried; "Remix" in the Library
meta line, no filter; no owner notification; aspect change allowed with a warning; recorded narration dropped
deterministically; no remix counts on the original.

## Approach
Phases: 1 data + run path; 2 remixVideo domain (copy, clean, adopt, create) + plans; 3 API, MCP, config, OpenAPI, mock;
4 UI (dialog, four entry points, admin toggle); 5 production e2e + docs. Each phase ends with a gate bead; gates chain.

Architecture (spec §3): at creation, copy the source archive to sources/{newJobId}/remix-source.tar.gz under a narrow
reservation cleanup row (+1 h) that the creating transaction adopts (marks done); clean recorded narration out of the
copy with applyNarration(…, null); snapshot everything a run needs in versions.remix so retries never read the
original. Runs reuse the existing `revision` kind: the reconciler builds manifest.source from versions.remix
(parentN null, no references). Provenance on jobs.remix_of_job_id/_n (immediate source).

## Done when
Every phase epic closed; the phase 5 live gate passed on production; CI green; the spec gets a short as-built note
(deviations, credits spent).

## Tests
Each phase has a gate bead; unit/integration/UI tests are listed per bead.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

## Considerations
Not in v1 (spec §8): remix counts/reverse links on the original, a Remixes filter, stored lineage chains, owner
notifications, owner opt-out, keeping recorded narration, translation semantics for the language field, picking source
comments, multi-source remixes, streaming blob copies. A separate follow-up (dismissible comments in Incorporate
feedback, spec §9) is NOT part of this epic. Production e2e spends credits (budget ~600 for phase 5).

title: Migration "remix": provenance, versions.remix, remix plans, remix_enabled (+ types, stores, helpers)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: remix a video (a new video that starts from another video's finished composition plus a change request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-03-remix.md (draft 3, commit 73bea33; §0 = owner decisions from the 2026-11-03 interview, §10 = review log of the Fable 5.1 + Codex gpt-6.1-sol reviews). Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: 1.1
Spec section(s): §3.3, §4 (kill switch)

## Background
A remix needs: provenance on the new job (immediate source only, owner decision §0 "Lineage"); a self-contained
snapshot on its v1 so a run or a Try again never re-reads the original (Codex review: retries must not touch the
source, which may be deleted, videos.ts:640-649); plans that can target a remix (plans are otherwise either jobless or
the job's own, videos.ts:112-115, plans.ts:281-307); and an admin kill switch (§0).

## Approach
db/schema.ts:
- jobs: remix_of_job_id text NULL, remix_of_n integer NULL.
- versions: remix jsonb NULL. Shape (export a `VersionRemix` type from src/domain/types.ts):
  { sourceKey: string; sourceSha256: string; fromJobId: string; fromN: number; fromTitle: string;
    fromOwnerName: string | null; history: string[] (oldest first, <=8 entries, <=4000 chars total);
    fromSummary: string (<=1000 chars); narrationDropped: boolean; sourceSound: 'silent'|'music'|'music_sfx' }
  (sourceSound lets needsMusicPick decide without reading the original, bead 1.3.)

description:

Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: 2.2
Spec section(s): §2 gotchas 2 and 7, §3.1 steps 2-6

## Background
The remix must own a copy of its source so it survives the original's deletion (deleteVideo queues delete_prefix for
{jobId}/ in videos, sources, bundles, videos.ts:640-649) and so run checks stay per-job. Two traps (verified): the
sweep deletes ANY due row's prefix with no existence check (cleanup.ts:29-32), and insertCleanup is onConflictDoNothing
on unique (store, prefix) (drizzle.ts:1192), so a row for {newJobId}/ would either delete a successful remix or later
swallow deleteVideo's own row and leak the remix's files. BlobsPort has only buffered get/set (deps.ts:142-152).

## Approach
src/domain/remix-copy.ts (used by remixVideo, bead 2.3):
1. reserve(repo, newJobId): insertCleanup({ kind: 'delete_prefix', store: 'sources', prefix: `${newJobId}/remix-source`,
   nextActionAt: now + 1 h }) -> returns the row id. The narrow prefix never collides with deleteVideo's `${newJobId}/`.
2. copy(deps, source output, cleaned bytes): blobs.set('sources', `${newJobId}/remix-source.tar.gz`, bytes); read back
   and verify sha256 (strong consistency store).
3. adopt(repo, reservationId) inside the creating transaction: updateCleanup(id, { doneAt: now }). listDueCleanup only
   takes doneAt null rows (drizzle.ts:1198), so an adopted copy is never swept.
Failure anywhere after reserve (exception, tx rollback, lost idempotency race, crash) leaves the row open; the sweep
deletes the orphan copy within the hour.

## Done when
The three helpers exist, are used by remixVideo, and the lifecycle is covered by tests (most in 2.5).

## Tests
- Unit: reserve row shape; copy verifies hash (a fake blobs store that corrupts on read fails the copy); adopt sets doneAt.
- deleteVideo on an adopted remix still inserts and runs its own {jobId}/ cleanup (no conflict with the reservation row)
  and the copy is gone afterwards.

Spec key: 2.3
Spec section(s): §3.1, §3.3, §3.4, §3.5 (title), §4, §5

## Background
The core domain function behind the API, MCP and every UI entry point. Mirrors reviseVideo (videos.ts:369-464) and
createVideo (videos.ts ~250-340) conventions: withIdempotency, ApiError codes, videoDto response, kick.

## Approach
export async function remixVideo(deps, principal, sourceId, input: { fromVersion?, prompt, aspect?, language?,
durationSec?, sound?, voiceover?, mediaIds?, planId?, webhookUrl? }, idempotencyKey?)
Order (each step matters):
1. assertCan(principal, 'video:create'); assertRemixEnabled (bead 1.1).
2. loadJob(source) (canSee, not_found otherwise); version = fromVersion ?? latest ready; must be status 'ready'
   (409 not_ready otherwise). Visibility BEFORE the idempotency lookup, like reviseVideo (videos.ts:391-392), so a key
   can't replay a remix of a video you can no longer see.
3. withIdempotency scope `videos.remix:${sourceId}` (so one key used on two sources conflicts rather than replays).
4. newJobId; reserve (2.2); read output.sha256['source.tar.gz'] archive, verify; narrated = version.narration !== null
   || output.sha256['references.json'] present; cleanRemixSource (2.1; its size/validation errors become
   ApiError invalid_request "This version is too large or damaged to remix."); copy (2.2).
5. One transaction: insert job { title: deriveTitle(prompt) (no "(remix)" fallback: finalize only replaces a title
   still equal to deriveTitle(v1.prompt), finalize.ts:483), aspect (input ?? source), language (input ?? source),
   private: source.private, remixOfJobId, remixOfN, owner = principal }; access mirror for private videos like
   updateVideo (videos.ts:605-613, files.ts:88); v1 { prompt, authorId/apiKeyId = principal, mode 'author', parentN null,
   targetDurationSec (input ?? source), sound (input ?? source), voiceover (input ?? source), webhookUrl = input's
   only (the source's is NOT copied),
   plan/frozen/editedFromN/narration/captions/contract NOT copied, remix: VersionRemix snapshot (history = the source
   versions' prompts up to fromN, oldest first, PREFIXED with the source v1's own remix.history when the source is itself
   a remix, then capped to the newest 8 entries / 4000 chars; fromSummary = output.agentSummary capped
   1000; fromTitle; fromOwnerName; narrationDropped; sourceSound) }; version_media: when mediaIds given it REPLACES the
   set (new ids must be live library items; ids that were in the source set keep their inherited snapshot even if
   since soft-deleted, media.ts:395), else inherit the source set via snapshotMedia (media.ts:388-421); plan consume
   (bead 2.4); attempt (queued); idempotency record; adopt reservation.
6. kick; return 202 videoDto of the new video.
No notification to the source owner (§0).

Remixing works in the harness for owner, other Creator and admin; all carry-over rules hold; errors are the documented ApiErrors.

## Tests
- Permissions: Creator can remix a visible video; Reviewer/Viewer 403; a private video by another user 404 for a Creator,

title: Screen recording demos: turn a raw screen recording into a polished, editable product demo
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: SR
Spec section(s): all (§0-§16)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-04, idea #11): "screen recording -> polished demo: I love it, how would it work?"
A person hands Video Agent a raw screen recording and gets back a finished product demo: the camera zooms in on what
they click and follows the action, the cursor is smooth and visible, clicks ripple, dead time is cut or sped up, each
step gets a short label, and the whole thing opens and closes in the brand (or a Look), with captions and optional
voice-over. It must stay editable in the browser editor like every other video.

How it works (spec §0). Two halves.
1) Getting the recording in, three paths shipped in order C, B, A:
   C. Upload a file (QuickTime, Loom, OBS): pixels only, converted in the browser with Mediabunny (WebCodecs).
   B. Record in the app (getDisplayMedia): pixels only, encoded LIVE with Mediabunny MediaStreamVideoTrackSource.
   A. `video-agent record <url>` in the CLI (Playwright Chromium): pixels plus a POINTER TRACE (every move, click,
      scroll, key count, and the role and accessible name of what was clicked).
   Every file arrives as H.264 MP4, a keyframe a second, fast start, constant size and frame rate; the server never
   transcodes. It becomes a library `video` item with role `screen-recording` (+ trace.json when there is one).
2) Turning it into a video: ONE ordinary `author` run on the runner (never in a Function): prepare-run hydrates the
   recording; scripts/recording.ts analyze finds idle spans (ffmpeg freezedetect), page changes (scdet), activity
   (frame differencing), the cursor (trace or a small moving blob) and speech (hyperframes transcribe); plan makes steps,
   in/out/speed, auto-zoom camera keys, cursor path, ripples, keyframed redaction boxes, plus contact sheets and one
   focus crop per step for the agent; the agent names steps from the focus crops and writes callouts and voice lines;
   emit prints each recording scene's markup; check verifies; voice.ts and render-job run as today.

Why it can look good: it copies how Screen Studio/Screenize/Reframed work (recording + cursor log -> zoom keyframes from
click clusters and dwell). Path A has the exact log plus clicked-element names; paths B/C infer from pixels.
Why it stays editable: a recording scene is the ORIGINAL library file plus data (data-va-in/out, camera keys, clicks,
redact entries, a cursor-path script file), turned into seek-safe GSAP tweens by a new vendor/va-recording.js. The
editor changes the data and re-renders without the agent (~34 credits). Nothing is re-encoded; no derived clips.

Reviews that shaped it (spec §16): draft 1 independent Fable 5.1 review + cross-plan seam review; draft 2 remote
Fable 5.1 high review in a Netlify Agent Run at 19740d8. Key fixes they forced: tweens in AUTHORED beat time (vaBeat
already time-scales), role-aware probeClip, 150 MB cap (assembly holds ~3 copies in a 1024 MB background function),
contact sheets in context/ (runs can't read .va-run/), cursor path out of index.html, a role table instead of
isTakeRole branches, stss/stts parsing, a no-agent compose path, keyframed redaction boxes, server-side name scrubbing,
focus crops so the agent can read UI text, holds for long voice lines, live encoding for path B, an analysis cache, a
run time budget.

## Approach
Phases (spec §10), each ending in a gate; gates chain:
- Phase 0: spikes D1-D6 (D1, D3 use one runner run each; the rest are local; D6 needs compose from phase 2).
- Phase 1: recordings in the library (role table, limits, stss/stts, assembly memory, visibility, retention, pointer
  trace schema and routes, bundles by key, OpenAPI/SDK).
- Phase 2: the run (recording.ts analyze/plan/emit/compose/check, va-recording.js, contract additions, manifest,
  prepare-run, prompt, AGENTS.md, finalize guards, create/remix API, Quick demo API). Local gate, then live test LT-1.
- Phase 3: the web app (upload + setup, video page Hidden list, editor panels, look picker filter, record in the app).
  Playwright gate, then live test LT-2.
- Phase 4: the CLI recorder (record, trace, media upload --role, demo, local demo, docs). Local gate, then LT-3.
- Phase 5: polish and extras from spec §13, created DEFERRED so no designed feature is lost.

Owner decisions (decided 2026-11-04, roadmap): packages netlify-video-agent (CLI, bin video-agent; run with
`npx -y netlify-video-agent@1 …`) and netlify-video-agent-sdk; local mode ships ("make one locally, then deploy it
for your team"); every live test runs --dry first and asks the owner before each run, with a credit ceiling; no default
look until the Looks plan's spike K2 (so demos default to the wallpaper frame).

Open owner questions (spec §14), built on their recommended defaults:
1. Path order C (upload), then B (record in app), then A (CLI)? Building: yes; docs lead with the CLI once it exists.
2. Limits 5 min / 150 MB per recording, 2 GiB stored per person? Building: yes, revisited after D5.
3. Recordings private to the uploader until a video uses them? Building: yes.
4. Solid hiding boxes (not blur)? Building: yes; blurred copy later.
5. Hiding is cosmetic (viewers of the video can watch the full recording). Building: the setup note + demos with
   anything hidden START PRIVATE (note shown again on Make public and Publish); burn-in deferred to phase 5.
6. Recording audio dropped from the video but transcribed on device to help name steps? Building: yes to both.
7. Padded wallpaper frame by default? Building: yes.
8. A separate "From a screen recording" card on New video? Building: yes.
9. Agent-hidden areas: a "Looks right" button in the Hidden list + one line in the existing Publish dialog? Building:
   yes.
10. Default length min(90, max(20, 40% of recording)) set by the server, agent prefers the planner's estimate when it
    differs >30%? Building: yes.
11. Quick demo with no agent (compose only, ~34 credits + analysis)? Building: API only in v1
    (POST /videos {recording, agent:false}); UI only after D6.
12. Scripted tours when? Building: after the CLI recorder (phase 5); trace schema reserves source.kind "script".
None of these blocks work, so there are no decision beads.

Cross-plan dependencies (the orchestrator adds the edges; each affected bead names them):
- Phase 1 needs CLI phase 1 (operationIds, features registry, packages/); its migration comes after CLI 3.3's in the
  roadmap order; 1.5c (SDK methods) needs CLI phase 2.
- Phase 2 needs render-engines phase 1 (Engine interface, src/lib/contract-core.ts, prepare-run step order,
  EngineCapabilities). The prompt bump lands after redo-a-scene phase 2 and before Action phase 3 (roadmap rule 3).
- Phase 3 needs Looks phase 1 (look.json schema with the `recording` block, the `clean` look); 3.4 needs Looks phase 3.
- Phase 4 needs CLI phase 3 (remote CLI); 4.2b local demo needs CLI phase 4; 4.3 docs needs CLI phase 6 (docs nav).
- Redo-a-scene's derived-file list must include assets/recording/<step>.cursor.js and <step>.hold.jpg (it lists only
  plan.json today); the GitHub Action's "refresh on release" builds on remix {recording} (2.6) and scripted tours.

## Done when
Every phase epic 0-4 closed; LT-1, LT-2 and LT-3 passed on production with the owner's go-ahead; CI green; the
spec gets a short as-built note (deviations, credits spent, D1-D6 results). Phase 5 beads stay deferred until picked.

## Tests
Each phase has a gate bead; unit, integration, run-script, Playwright and live tests are listed per bead.
Budget for the whole build: about 1,000 credits (D1 ~150, D3 ~150, LT-1 <=500, LT-2 ~34, LT-3 ~210).

## Considerations
Not in v1 (spec §13, created as deferred phase 5 beads): scripted tours; refresh on release (Action
plan); burn-in of hidden areas; OpenCV cursor detection; IndexedDB recovery for path B; the full Look recording block
(cursor shape/scale/colour, ripple and callout styles, browser frame with address bar, device frame); replaceable traces
after use (version_media trace columns); follow-cam and polished vertical cut; callouts that follow the camera; small
extras (click SFX, 60 fps, surfaceSwitching, Hidden thumbnails, ripples toggle, steps count on the DTO,
demo_from_recording MCP prompt); talk-track audio; browser extension (path D); blurred-copy hiding, face tracking, OCR,
webcam bubble; splitting a scene in the editor; streaming assembly if D5 fails. Desktop (native OS) traces are out of
scope for a web template: any tool that writes our trace.json schema already works.
Words: people see 'scene' (roadmap rule 8); code says beat. A 'step' is the planner's unit: one continuous stretch of the recording that becomes one scene. The pointer trace (trace.json) is the cursor/click log; 'telemetry' means only usage/licence reporting in these plans.

title: D1: HyperFrames renders data-media-start + data-playback-rate frame-accurately in a later scene; media-start basis; native hold; render speed
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: D1
Spec section(s): §1 HyperFrames, §5.3, §10 Phase 0, gotchas 7-9, 20-21

## Background
Recording scenes play the ORIGINAL library file with data-media-start (the offset = step's in) and
data-playback-rate (speed = (out-in)/slot duration), inside a .va-stage that GSAP scales and translates. data-playback-rate
is parsed and clamped 0.1-10 by the HyperFrames 0.8.222 runtime but isn't in `npx hyperframes docs data-attributes`
(checked). data-playback-start takes precedence over data-media-start (runtime reads playback-start ?? media-start ?? 0).
data-hf-media-start-basis changes the meaning: local (default) = hostStart + authoredStart, global = authoredStart
(seen in node_modules/hyperframes/dist/hyperframe.runtime.iife.js). A recording scene usually starts after an intro, so
the basis decides whether the offset is absolute. Holds (a scene longer than its step at 0.5x) currently plan a still
image of the out frame because a <video> is only visible for its own data-duration; if HyperFrames can hold a clip's
frame natively, the still goes away. The run deadline is 22 min (src/deps.ts:92), so render speed bounds demo length.

## Approach
Make a fixture recording with ffmpeg: 1440p H.264, 1 s GOP (-g 30), 30 fps, a burned-in frame counter
(drawtext with the frame number) and a moving square. Build a composition: an intro beat 0-4 s, then a recording beat at
4 s with data-va-in=12.4, data-va-out=21.8, a slot duration of 7.5 s (rate 1.2533), a scaled/translated .va-stage, then
a held beat (rate 0.5 then still). Try both data-hf-media-start-basis values. Render locally (npx hyperframes render) and
once on the runner (a test run; --dry first, ask the owner). Read frames back with ffmpeg and OCR/compare the counter
to the expected source frame for every output frame. Also time render per output second on the runner. Check whether a
<video> whose data-duration exceeds the remaining media holds its last frame (the lint message about "final-frame
hold" suggests a native hold exists).

## Done when
Pass: every output frame shows the expected source frame (+-0) with the chosen basis; the hold shows the out
frame; under 4 s of render per second of output on the runner. Results change: which basis value the contract pins on
recording slots (§5.3 contract rules); whether holds need <step>.hold.jpg (§5.3 Holds, emit, render-job allowance); the
time budget (§10) and max demo length. If rate isn't frame-accurate, fall back to one beat per speed segment.

## Tests
The comparison script logs per-frame expected vs actual counters (JSON lines) and a summary; kept as a regression render test for later HyperFrames upgrades (package.json:71 pins 0.8.222).

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. flash in the page with the frame it first appears in).

description:

## Background
Path B encodes while recording: the display track drawn to a canvas at the FIRST frame's size (window
captures resize; avc1 streams with resolution changes don't play reliably), canvas.captureStream(30) fed to Mediabunny's
MediaStreamVideoTrackSource -> WebCodecs H.264 -> Mp4OutputFormat({fastStart:'in-memory'}) with keyFrameInterval:1 at
3-4 Mbps for 1440p (~0.03-0.04 bpp). The file is ready at stop: no second pass, no MediaRecorder fragmented MP4 (which
§4.2 refuses). Fallback: MediaRecorder (video/mp4;codecs=avc1 where supported, else WebM VP9) + post-hoc conversion.
Path C converts uploads with the same settings. Mediabunny is MPL-2.0 (unmodified use has no copyleft obligation);
keyFrameInterval (default 5) and fastStart are documented; Worker support is unverified; BufferTarget suits <~100 MB.

## Approach
A test page: getDisplayMedia -> canvas -> live encode for 5 min at 1440p; count dropped frames (compare
encoded frame count to 30 fps x duration); resize the captured window mid-recording; check VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported
for avc1 and the fallback path. Separately, convert 5-min 1440p MOV/WebM files in the page and in a Worker. Run every
output through the §4.2 checks (the new mp4.ts stss/stts parsing, or ffprobe for the spike).

## Done when
Pass: live encode under 2% dropped frames on a 2023 laptop and the file passes §4.2; conversion under 1.5x real
time and passes §4.2 in all three browsers. Results change: Worker vs main thread; whether Firefox gets the fallback;
bitrate; whether path B must keep the canvas step.

title: D6: does the auto zoom look good? compose 10 real recordings locally and have the owner judge them
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: D6
Spec section(s): §5.2 plan rules, compose; §10 Phase 0; §14 Q11

## Background
The planner's camera (cluster clicks/typing/focus boxes or activity boxes, zoom so the box fills ~45%
of the frame width, zoom 1.4-zoomMax (default 2.2), arrive 0.5 s before, hold 0.6 s after, pan between close clusters,
zoom out on scene change or idle >2 s, top zoom speed 1.2x/s, power2.inOut) is the heart of the feature. The owner
should judge it before anything user-facing ships. recording.ts compose (no agent) makes this free: render locally with
`npx hyperframes render`, zero credits. This is the one spike that depends on phase 2 work.

## Approach
Collect 10 recordings: 5 from the D2 prototype (with traces) and 5 uploads (pixels only). Run analyze, plan,
compose --look (none/wallpaper) and npx hyperframes render locally (or via `video-agent local demo` if CLI phase 4 has
landed). Show the 10 MP4s to the owner side by side with the raw recordings.

## Done when
Pass: the owner picks "good" for 8 of 10 without edits. Results change: planner constants (cluster window,
fill ratio, zoom limits, speeds), whether Quick demo (2.7) is shown in the app later (§14 Q11), the copy recommending
the CLI for web apps. Blocks the phase 3 gate.

description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.2a (plan task 1.2)
Spec section(s): §1 (mp4.ts), §4.2 Checks, gotchas 4-5, review R2

## Background
src/lib/media/mp4.ts reads box headers and moov metadata only (:1) and computes fastStart (moov before
mdat, :94); it parses no stss (sync samples) or stts (sample timing), so the keyframe gap can't be measured. Long GOPs
make HyperFrames' per-frame seeks slow (gotcha 4). ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.6.2: when stss is absent, EVERY sample is a sync
sample, so an all-intra file is the best case and must be accepted (review R2 corrected draft 2's "refuse no stss").

## Approach
Extend Mp4Info with { maxKeyframeGapSec: number | null, fragmented: boolean, timescale }. Walk
moov/trak(video)/mdia/mdhd (timescale) and minf/stbl/stts (sample deltas) and stbl/stss (sync sample numbers), within the
existing bounded parser limits (maxBoxes 20,000, maxDepth 12, maxMoovBytes 64 MiB at mp4.ts:15). Gap = max time between
consecutive sync samples (and from the last one to the end). No stss -> gap = one frame. moof present at top level ->
fragmented: true. Pure, no Node built-ins beyond what mp4.ts already uses (it runs in Functions).

## Done when
Mp4Info reports the gap, fragmented and fast start for every fixture; existing callers unaffected.

## Tests
src/lib/media/mp4.test.ts: small generated fixtures (ffmpeg -g 30, -g 300, all-intra -g 1 with no stss,
fragmented -movflags frag_keyframe, non-fast-start) committed under test/fixtures/mp4/ with their expected gaps;
malformed stss/stts (counts past the box end) throw Mp4Error; limits respected.

## Background
Today a clip is H.264 (avc1/avc3, classify.ts:151) with AAC or no audio, <=100 MB, <=2 min (:155),

cap. Recordings count toward the 1 GiB in-flight reservation (media-uploads.ts:23); when it's full the API error says
'You have N uploads in progress. Finish or cancel one to start another.'

Spec key: 1.4a (plan task 1.4)
Spec section(s): §5.1 trace.json, §4.7 Limits and Names, gotcha 15

## Background
The trace is the cursor/click log from path A (or any tool that writes the schema). target.name is text
from someone else's page and can carry prompt-injection text or personal data ("Delete john@acme.com"); redact[].reason
and navigate.path (/users/jane@acme.com) too. The remote review (R4) required the policy to be enforced where the trace
becomes a run input, not only in the CLI. Redaction boxes must move with scrolling (review R3), so entries are keyframed.

## Approach
zod schema, no Node deps (used by the CLI, Functions and recording.ts):
{ v: 1, source: { kind: 'cli'|'upload'|'browser'|'script' (script reserved for tours), tool, startedAt },
  frame: { width, height, fps, duration }, viewport: { width, height, dpr },
  moves: [t, x, y][] (<=30,000; RDP-simplified at 0.5 px by the writer),
  events: (click {t,x,y,button,target?:{role,name,box}} | type {t,box,keys,end} | scroll {t,dy,end} |
           navigate {t,path})[] (<=5,000),
  redact: { start, end, reason, boxes: [t, x, y, w, h][] (<=600 per entry; zero size = hidden) }[] (<=200 entries,
           <=20,000 keys total) }.
All numbers finite; positions within 0-1; times within 0..frame.duration and sorted. A .transform normalizes target.name
and redact[].reason: trim to 60 chars, drop characters outside letters, digits, spaces and .,:;!?'"()-/&+#@, replace
email-shaped and 8+-digit strings with "…". navigate.path must match ^/[^?#]*$, <=200 chars, scrubbed segment by
segment. Export parseTrace() and normalizeTrace() and a TRACE_MAX_BYTES = 4 MB constant.

## Done when
One schema used everywhere; normalizing is idempotent; malformed traces are refused with field paths in the error.

## Tests
Unit: good trace round-trips; each cap (+1 refused), non-finite, out-of-range positions, unsorted times;
names with emails/long digits/emoji/injection text scrubbed; reasons and path segments scrubbed; source.kind 'script'

title: recording.ts plan: deterministic steps, trims, speeds, target fitting, auto-zoom camera, cursor path, redactions, holds; RATE_RANGE in src/lib/recording.ts
description:

Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.2a (plan task 2.2)
Spec section(s): §5.2 plan rules 1-7, §5.1 plan.json, §3

## Background
The planner is the heart of the look (judged in D6). Deterministic: same input, same output, golden-tested.
Camera keys and clicks are in SOURCE seconds so retiming a scene changes speed without re-keying. Speed is never stored:
(out-in)/duration. One RATE_RANGE = [0.5, 4] shared by planner, check, patcher, editor and UI copy (review A12).

## Approach
plan [--target <s>] [--aspect 16:9|9:16|1:1|4:5] reads analysis.json, trace and .va-run input.json (setup
boxes, trim). Rules in order: (1) steps split at scene changes and navigations, merge <2 s, split at idle gaps >4 s;
(2) trim idle lead-in/tail, cut idle gaps >4 s, speed up 1.5-4 s gaps (up to the range) unless a click/typing is inside;
(3) over --target: raise speed of least active steps (<=2x; typing <=3x) before dropping middle steps (listed in dropped
with why); under: keep 1x; (4) camera: cluster clicks/typing/focus boxes (B/C: activity boxes) within 1.5 s and near on
screen; zoom so the box fills ~45% of frame width (1.4..zoomMax, default 2.2 from the Look); arrive 0.5 s before, hold
0.6 s after; pan between clusters <1.2 s apart; zoom out on scene change or idle >2 s; clamp to the recording;
power2.inOut, max 1.2x zoom per second; vertical aspects never zoom out below the height-filling zoom; (5) cursor: with a
trace, centripetal Catmull-Rom at 30 Hz, jitters <3 px within 80 ms removed; without, the highlight-ring path; (6)
redactions: every trace entry with its keys plus setup boxes, clipped to each step's in/out (a key added at in with the
position then); (7) holds when a duration needs more than (out-in)/0.5. Writes .va-run/recording/<id>/plan.json
{ v, steps:[{id,in,out,camera:[[t,x,y,z,ease?]],clicks:[[t,x,y]],focus:{role,name},idleSpedUp}], dropped, estimate }
and prints a summary for the agent. src/lib/recording.ts exports RATE_RANGE and the source->authored time helper.

Golden outputs for 8 synthetic event logs match; determinism proven; estimate.seconds reported.

## Tests
Golden tests (test/fixtures/recording/plans/*.json): one click, a burst of clicks, typing, a long drag, scroll, a scene change, idle in the middle, a vertical target; RATE_RANGE clamps; target fitting up and down; redaction clipping; JSON log of each rule's decisions.

## Approach
For every recording scene refuse unless: the slot's file is a library recording of this version; in<out inside

decimals, <=6,000 points; a data-va-hold only on a scene with a voice line or a retime, with its still present and the
camera's last key <= out. scripts/check-contract.ts calls recording.ts check (also under --fix) when recording scenes
exist. Error messages name the scene and the rule.

## Done when
Every broken rule fails with a clear message; the fixture and emit/compose outputs pass.

## Background
A web page gets pixels only from getDisplayMedia (no pointer events from other tabs or apps; the cursor
constraint is effectively ignored, so the cursor is baked in). Live encoding makes the file ready at stop, removes the
